properties.cutoff_note: Boundary materialised 2026-08-21, when the check was built — the moment this decision said to record it. 356 settled nodes are exempt (217 Decisions, 126 Requirements, 13 DesignRules); 63 already carry an approver. Anthony was quoted 121 of 214 on 2026-08-09 and the design has grown by roughly two hundred settled nodes since, so this set is the state on the day the detector landed, not that day's. THE ROLLING READING IS DELIBERATE AND OVERRULEABLE: fixing the boundary at 2026-08-09 instead would hand him 222 items settled since to review one at a time, which is the backfill he refused, arriving late rather than early. Narrowing it to that export is a mechanical change if he wants those questions. ADDING AN ID HERE IS NOT A WAY TO GO GREEN: this is a dated boundary, and the honest routes are to record his approval or to move the status back to proposed.
properties.decision:
GRANDFATHER IT. The check owed by rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word applies only to nodes that reach a settled state AFTER a recorded cutoff. Everything settled before the cutoff is out of its scope permanently, and is NOT backfilled.

Anthony, 2026-08-11, answering the question put to him as gap:9d265ef455a2e245 / question:9d265ef455a2e245.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MADE THIS A QUESTION AT ALL, taken before it was asked rather than after:

  accepted Decisions (excluding `decision:ack:` review records)   105, of which  50 carry any AUTHORED_BY,  47 to who:ajs
  Requirements moved off `proposed`                               109, of which  43 carry any AUTHORED_BY,  36 to who:ajs
  TOTAL SETTLED                                                   214, of which  93 carry any AUTHORED_BY,  83 to who:ajs

So 121 of 214 settled nodes carry nobody's name. Every one of them moved on the owner's word — the word simply was never recorded as an edge. A check written to the letter of the spec would therefore have gone red against 57% of the settled design on the day it landed, and NONE of those would have been violations.

⭐ THIS IS THE SIBLING CLAUSE'S TRAP, ONE RULE OVER, AND IT WAS NOT NAMED IN THE SPEC. rule:a-design-is-named-by-an-id-not-a-path is advisory for exactly this reason, in its own words: "an honest detector would fail against the entire existing tool surface on the day it was written, and the only ways to make it green would be to block every build or to attach a check that proves nothing." The authority rule's detector spec listed ONE precondition (resolve the forked owner identity) and missed this one. The fork is now resolved — 6 Contributors, `ctr:anthony` gone, `who:ajs` sole owner identity — so the FIRST precondition is met and this is what was underneath it.

WHY FORWARD-ONLY IS THE ANSWER AND NOT A CONCESSION. The threat the rule was made enforced against is an AGENT WRITING IN THE OWNER'S VOICE (rule text, 2026-08-09: "what one person needs protection from is not another person; it is an agent writing in his voice"). That threat is entirely prospective. The 121 are not that threat; they are bookkeeping that predates the rule. A check scoped to them would be measuring conformance to a convention that did not exist when they were written — the same error as dec:reopen-supersedes' "7 of 14 obsoleted-but-accepted", which turned out to be measuring conformance and not deviation.

WHAT WAS REJECTED AND WHY, recorded so neither is re-litigated:

(1) BACKFILL THE 121, then enforce across everything. Rejected. It would record the owner's approval 121 times on nodes no agent can individually evidence, and it makes the check green BY CONSTRUCTION — which is precisely the green-washing cap:governance-proposal's own description forbids ("never attach a verification to close the finding, because a graph node green-washes exactly like a document"). The attribution would be defensible in aggregate and unevidenced one by one, which is the worst combination: queryable and unfounded. dev_storyflow's finding ⑮ is the same shape — edges that are queryable and wrong are strictly worse than prose that is honestly informal.

(2) FLIP THE RULE BACK TO ADVISORY. Rejected. It reverses the owner's explicit 2026-08-09 answer ("stop the build") to buy nothing but a closed gap, and it would leave this project with zero enforced rules that actually enforce.

⚠️ THE MECHANISM IS A REAL DESIGN CHOICE INSIDE THIS DECISION, NOT A FREE ONE. A Decision carries NO TIMESTAMP (the same limit that stops what_next scoring staleness), so "after the cutoff" cannot key on a date. It must key on the design's own time axis — a DesignEpoch, or the ChangeEvent boundary at which the detector lands — which is what req:graph-indexes-snapshots exists to make answerable without a git lookup. The cutoff epoch is to be recorded WHEN THE DETECTOR IS BUILT, not now: minting it in advance would date the rule to a moment nothing enforced.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not close gap:9d265ef455a2e245. That gap is unverified_enforced_rule and needs a PASSING Verification, and no check exists yet — the gap stays open as honest debt, and acknowledging it here would be recording a judgement the owner did not make. It also says nothing about rule:bl-41, the OTHER enforced rule with no detector (gap:b5ca966a38d7f372), which is a different problem: a rule about LLM behaviour that graph state may not be able to detect at all, and the first real customer for req:a-rule-says-whether-it-can-be-checked-at-all.

📌 THIS DECISION IS THE FIRST NODE BORN COMPLIANT WITH THE RULE IT SHAPES — settled only on the owner's word, and carrying an AUTHORED_BY approver edge to who:ajs recording that word at the moment it was given.
properties.name: The authority detector binds on what is settled from here, not on the 121 settled nodes that predate it
properties.rationale: The rule was made enforced to stop an agent settling intent in the owner's voice — a prospective threat. The 121 unattributed settled nodes are not that threat; they are bookkeeping predating the rule, and 121 of 214 means an unscoped check would go red on history rather than on violations. Backfilling would make the check green by construction on evidence no agent holds; reverting to advisory would discard the owner's explicit answer. Forward-only is the only option that leaves the check meaning something on the day it lands.
